text.content:
The "low rites" vary from pack to pack. Not every pack observes them, and those that do often put their own local spin on each one. Storytellers are free to establish their own Ignoblis Ritae, and players are encouraged to develop new low rites for their packs subject to review by their characters' superiors — the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.6868ee8c357f4b73]{Sabbat} rewards this kind of bottom-up innovation. See the companion Sabbat Rituals & Monomacy journal for the sect-wide Auctoritas Ritae.

Using the Ignoblis Ritae

Storytellers may grant temporary bonus Traits ("Gift Traits") to packs that observe a low rite appropriately — for example, a ritual of strength performed before battle might grant an extra Physical Trait for the duration of the anticipated fight. Gift Traits always require Storyteller approval and expire at the end of the specific task they were granted for.

Acceptance

Marks an individual's induction into a pack — whether at the end of the Auctoritas Creation Rites, on adoption of a Sabbat member separated from her old pack, or as a reaffirmation of the pack's membership after a change of leadership. Each pack member acknowledges the newcomer with a personal token (vitae, gifts, advice, favors, or something else useful). There is no innate magical benefit to Acceptance, only the social bond it cements. Many packs include a short oath in which the newcomer acknowledges her debt to the pack and the sect, and the pack in turn swears to treat her as an equal — sharing equally in rewards for her successes and punishments for her failures.

Allegiance

Bridges the gap between a vampire's formal creation as Sabbat and her full acceptance into a specific pack. The candidate must prove herself familiar with sect ideals and capable of acting effectively, occupying a distinctly junior position in the meantime: she stands at the rear during Auctoritas rites, drinks last (and usually cannot contribute her own blood) at the Vaulderie, and may not take part in discussions of the Book of Nod. Most packs apply a secret mark identifying her as still-in-progress. The trial period can run a few weeks for an exceptional candidate or stretch for years; a vampire who never wins her pack's confidence risks Final Death at the hands of her own creators. @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.fc464242d84d4e34]{Camarilla} defectors face longer scrutiny and tougher loyalty tests, often including attacks on their former associates.

The Asp's Blessing

Plays out a common Sabbat metaphor — the sect as serpent — literally. The priest raises a (usually venomous) snake before the pack and asks Caine's spirit to guide its eyes and fangs. Each member steps forward to kiss the snake; if it bites, the priest denounces that vampire for concealed sins. Examination and a Contrition rite follow for anyone who fails this test of purity.

Contrition

Among the most common low rites, and one of the likeliest to eventually earn Auctoritas standing. A Sabbat member who has wronged the sect confesses her failings and accepts any punishment short of Final Death. Minor offenses might earn no more than a beating and unpleasant duties; breaches of sect security can mean dismemberment, with just enough vitae restored afterward to let the contrite vampire begin healing. Packs vary in how willing they are to accept repeated Contrition for the same offense (or a sustained pattern of misconduct) — and leaders who show too much leniency risk condemnation themselves, since the sect considers itself perpetually at war.

Welcoming

A social rite performed whenever two packs meet for a shared task, or a nomadic pack enters a new city, to establish neutral ground and let members become acquainted. Members introduce themselves and their homes; anyone with an existing grievance against another participant speaks up, and the packs' ducti and priests attempt to mediate (sometimes via a short, non-lethal duel). Leaders set basic protocols for havens and feeding grounds, and everyone reaffirms loyalty to the Sabbat's twin principles of individual liberty and united action. Some areas have pack leaders exchange blood; more devout ones may have everyone share a full Vaulderie on the spot. Afterward, the packs' leaders are free to plan their common purpose.

Thanksgiving

A literal rite of giving thanks: the pack gathers, each member thanks Caine for his favor, and then recounts a story of a recent accomplishment meant to show off his strength, cunning, or other prized quality (with exaggeration being the norm in most packs that practice this). Thanksgiving often precedes an esbat or other formal occasion.

Martial

An umbrella term for low rites meant to muster a pack's enthusiasm and ability for the Sabbat's endless war against its enemies. A Martial rite typically involves some rhythmic activity — music, dance, or martial arts — to ease participants into a trance state. Traditional or neo-primitive packs incorporate body adornment and ritual scarification.

Spilling of Blood

One of several low rites that never quite achieved Auctoritas status despite being well-known sect-wide. Vampires feeding together trade sips from each other's vessels with a ritual acknowledgement, e.g. "Hot blood that spurted from Abel at his time of death, sustain us for the will of the Sabbat."

Stealth

Practiced by packs about to undertake an assignment requiring silence, or simply to test their discipline. Participants bite out each other's tongues and spit the severed organs into a fire; the wound inflicts no lasting damage. Sometimes the ductus or priest abstains so she can still give verbal orders, while everyone else communicates via hand signals and mental Disciplines for the remainder of the rite.

System: Each participant who has her tongue bitten out spends one Blood Point to stabilize the wound.

Sun Dance

Tests participants' endurance and courage. Always performed during a full moon: participants don frightening costumes or body paint and dance from waking at sunset until sunrise around a symbolic inscription of a fiery sun, then attempt to stay awake and out in the open as long as possible into the new day. A Blood Feast typically follows the next night. Some packs arrange to rescue participants too injured to seek shelter in time; others don't, though sect leaders frown on pointless losses and encourage at least having observers on hand.

Tests of Pain

A family of rites that challenge a participant's ability to stay functional through severe pain. Some packs use Tests of Pain to help choose new leaders; many pair them with Contrition rites as punishment. Common variants include the Trial by Stake (the subject is staked to a wall through the chest, feet off the ground, left until packmates release her near sunrise or until she tears free to perform further tests), the Trial by Fire (the pack priest applies flame to parts of the subject's body), and the Trial by Gauntlet (the subject runs between two rows of packmates who beat her, sometimes with weapons, sometimes barehanded). Pack priests generally develop their own favored repertoire of tests.

System: Use Courage and Self-Control (or Instinct) tests for individual Tests of Pain whenever a vampire's resolve is in doubt.

Truth Revealed

Hangs near the edge of Auctoritas standing; its reliability depends on the skill of the administering priest. A vampire suspected of dishonesty writes a statement in her own blood; the priest burns the paper in a ceremonial censer. Black smoke indicates the statement was false, white smoke indicates truthfulness — and the rite produces accurate results more often than chance alone would explain, which Sabbat scholars attribute to the pack's latent mystic power when united in a search for truth.

System: A priest with three or more levels of Occult or Rituals may make a Mental Challenge against the subject of the inquiry; if the priest succeeds, the rite always produces the correct color of smoke.
